title: Democratic Republic of the Congo Visa Application
description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ministère des Affaires Étrangères et Coopération Internationale (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation) "Formulaire de Demande de Visa / Visa Application Form", a bilingual (French/English) consular visa application filed by a foreign national through a Congolese embassy or consulate abroad. Opens the Democratic Republic of the Congo as the registry's 102nd jurisdiction, via the Visa vertical (1 of 6); DMV, Business Formation, Passport, Taxes, and National ID & Civic Documents remain open, unscreened backlog for a future cycle. This document models the applicant's identity, family, and contact particulars (Section B, Items 1–10); passport/travel-document details (Items 11–13); the purpose of travel and any place of mission (Items 14–15); the requested visa type (transit, single entry, two entries, or multiple entries) and its associated travel dates (Item 16 and Page 2); the applicant's most recent prior DRC visa, if any (Page 2, Item 1); whether the trip is sponsored by an inviting individual/legal entity or funded by the applicant's own means (Page 2, Items 2–3); the expected visa processing period (Item 4); and the applicant's declaration and signature (Item 5). It excludes the form's own "SECTION À REMPLIR PAR LA CHANCELLERIE / SECTION TO BE FILLED OUT BY CHANCERY" block, which is completed by embassy staff, not the applicant. Filing this application is a traveller action performed with a Congolese embassy or consulate; this schema does not file the application itself, and the live source is always authoritative. See VERIFICATION.md for the full sourcing record and every disclosed scoping decision. GovSchema is independent and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or operated by the Democratic Republic of the Congo or its Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation.

verification.notes:
GOV-5798 ("GovSchema Standard Research"), re-scouting a candidate first banked by GOV-5791 ("DR Congo Passport and Visa AcroForms", one of 16 countries scouted that cycle, none authored). Opens the Democratic Republic of the Congo as the registry's 102nd jurisdiction, via the Visa vertical (1 of 6). Source: https://www.ambardcusa.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/Visas_application_writable.pdf ("Formulaire de Demande de Visa / Visa Application Form", Ministère des Affaires Étrangères et Coopération Internationale, distributed by the Embassy of the Democratic Republic of the Congo in Washington, DC). Re-fetched directly: HTTP 200, Content-Type application/pdf, 601,971 bytes, sha256 ab7c73f01a0cbfdfc32d7bfed7abda4afb672757712e1a4d922219754c9d00cb, no login/CAPTCHA/WAF gate on the asset itself (the bare ambardcusa.org domain root now 301-redirects to ambadrcusa.org, but this direct asset path is unaffected). Confirmed mechanically via pdfjs-dist: a genuine AcroForm, 2 pages, 58 form-field annotations on page 1 and 25 on page 2 (83 raw widgets total).

Models 60 fields[] across 7 steps mirroring the form's own numbered sections (Section B Items 1–16 on page 1, continuing unnumbered onto page 2 before its own numbered Items 1–5), 3 documents[] entries (2 supporting documents from Section A's own attachment checklist, 1 attestation from the Item 5 declaration), and 1 crossFieldValidation rule (dateOfExpiration after dateOfIssue). See VERIFICATION.md for the full sourcing record and every disclosed finding, including: (1) this form carries no printed required/optional signal anywhere, so every field's requiredness is a disclosed domain judgment call; (2) two internal PDF field names are reused/mismatched across the document (the residency card's own Date d'expiration line is internally named 'voyage a specifier', reusing Item 11's field name; the Transit visa-type checkbox is internally named 'Aller Du', reusing its own first date sub-field's label) — disambiguated by rect position, not internal field name; (3) footnote (*3) has no inline reference point anywhere on the form and is not modelled, disclosed as an orphaned footnote rather than guessed; (4) hasSponsor is a directly-supplied boolean gate (the form itself has no yes/no checkbox distinguishing a sponsored from a self-funded traveller), the same convention as mt/identita/long-stay-visa-application's own hasHostInMalta; (5) the form's own chancery-only section is excluded as non-applicant-facing.

2 valid mock scenarios plus 8 mutation-control fixtures committed under conformance/cd/maeci/visa-application/1.0.0/. An ephemeral, from-scratch conformance checker ran all 10: both valid scenarios at 0 errors, all 8 mutation controls each raising exactly 1 error, 0 dangling requiredWhen references, and the crossFieldValidation rule holds on both valid scenarios. Validated clean with node tools/validate.mjs and node tools/validate-ajv.mjs, individually and as part of the full registry run. Opens Democratic Republic of the Congo's Visa vertical (1 of 6); DMV, Business Formation, Passport, Taxes, and National ID & Civic Documents remain open, unscreened backlog for a future cycle.
